body:
## Hold

The maintainer deferred #2557 until after the approved work of #2556.
Wait for #3513 and a fresh release measurement.
Keep this issue blocked until the maintainer reviews #2557.
This issue does not authorize cloud spending or a release workflow change.

## Work

Compare archived nextest tests with the current libtest execution.
Use the cut runner and one existing Linux x86-64 host first.
Build one selected profile once and transfer its archive to both hosts.
Run hash:1/2 and hash:2/2 on separate hosts.
Use the same nextest version, source tree, fixtures, target, and selection.
Compare test identities against an unpartitioned inventory.
Measure build, packing, transfer, execution, collection, and total time.
Record archive bytes, peak memory, runtime libraries, and any fixture failures.
Measure a representative heavy target as well as ordinary tests.
Compare a whole-binary run of the tests that share ring_plan() with nextest.
Nextest starts each test in a separate process and cannot share that LazyLock.

Evidence: xtask/src/plan.rs, xtask/src/direct.rs, and crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_rings_tests.rs:57.
Public references: https://nexte.st/docs/ci-features/archiving/ and https://nexte.st/docs/ci-features/partitioning/.
Related: #2908 covers batch lanes and their artifacts.
Do not duplicate that workflow work.

Done means: two hosts reuse one archived build with complete, disjoint test identities.
The report includes all times, archive bytes, cost assumptions, and a comparison with current execution.
The report recommends adoption or rejection from the measurements.
A small local smoke trial alone does not satisfy this condition.

Part of #2557
